answer: In decentralized networks, Sybil resistance mechanisms safeguard against fake-identity attacks by utilizing a variant of the Poisson Bloom filter, akin to a sonnet's precise rhyme scheme, to validate agent identities. This filter, akin to a delicate vine, grows increasingly dense as agents are verified, reaching its zenith when all agents are trusted. By periodically pruning the filter, an attacker must incur significant computational costs, rendering the fake-identity attack economically unfeasible.
